$comment: Mission 1.74.4. A replacement packet, because the recipient changed and the recipient is one of the bound fields. Version 1 is NOT edited: it recorded a correctly established address that later rejected delivery, which is a fact about the provider rather than an error in the record.
supersedes_note: v1 stays exactly as it was, still answering to its own hash. It is superseded because its recipient is unreachable, not because it was wrong.
subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites
body:
Do Globalping's Terms permit using the HTTP measurement API for bounded HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites, including as part of a commercial tool or commercial-purpose research workflow, provided the use complies with Globalping's limits and other policies?

I am asking because the Permitted Use section describes monitoring, debugging and benchmarking 'your internet infrastructure', while the Credits FAQ states that commercial use is supported within the limits of the Terms, and I did not want to read either beyond what it says.
why_no_explanatory_sentence_was_added: a line explaining that the designated address bounced was considered and NOT added. The operator's instruction was to preserve the approved text unless a change is strictly required, and nothing about the question changes with the recipient. Adding prose would make this a differently worded enquiry that the operator has not read.
why_the_channel_label_changed: v1 went to the address the Terms designate for Terms questions. This one goes to the address the provider publishes for general contact. Reusing the v1 label would assert a designation this address does not have.
first_party_channel_basis:
read from the provider's own committed website source, jsdelivr/globalping.io src/views/components/footer.html, as the live mailto link '
  • d@globalping.io
    • ', and corroborated by the rendered homepage. Established on provenance rather than on spelling, and reviewed in globalping-r2-replacement-recipient-review-v1.json.
why_public_documentation_is_insufficient: the Terms neither prohibit nor grant the activity, the one incorporating hook was followed and repeats the same narrow framing, and the Credits FAQ expressly defers to the Terms
expected_answer_discriminator: an answer stating that the current Terms do or do not cover measuring third-party publicly reachable targets maps directly to R2-B. A statement that a separate permission is needed maps to PROVIDER_TERMS_REQUIRE_CLARIFICATION rather than to a grant.
why: the Mission 1.74.2 approval binds approved_content_sha256, and this packet's digest differs because the recipient and channel differ. So the exhausted approval cannot name this document -- the hash is what defeats the hazard of a shared question_id, rather than a rule somebody has to remember.
